title: Evaluation of post-natal angiogenesis in a mouse hind limb ischemia model
protocol: Inject each mouse with preemptive analgesia intraperitoneally.
Use Altadol® at a final concentration of 5 mg/kg for injection.
Administer the injection 30 minutes before surgery and again 2- and 24 hours after induction of HLI.
Shave the limbs of the mouse.
Induce sedation by placing the animal in an induction chamber saturated with 5% isoflurane.
Transfer the animal to a surgical table in a supine position once sedated.
Deliver 1–3% isoflurane in 100% O2 at a flow rate of 1L/min through a mask to maintain anesthesia.
Disinfect the surgical table and instruments with ethanol 70%.
Shave hair from the ventral side of the hind limbs up to 0.5 cm above the groin using an electric shaver.
Apply a thin layer of hair removal cream for 2–3 minutes on the shaved area.
Gently remove excess hair removal cream with a paper towel dampened in warm water.
Keep the animal in a supine position with a mask delivering 1–3% isoflurane in 100% O2 at a flow rate of 1L/min.
Place the animal with its right side facing the operator for ischemia on the right hindlimb.
Extend the right limb by 90° and secure it by placing a piece of tape on the paw with the plantar side facing upwards.
Disinfect the surface of the animal's right limb using a cotton swab moistened with povidone/iodine.
Disinfect the surgical area using a paper towel embedded with 70% ethanol.
Make a small vertical incision at the level of the groin between the left inguinal fat pad and the peritoneum using fine forceps and surgical scissors.
Gently brush away the subcutaneous fat tissue surrounding the thigh muscle to separate the fat pad from the muscle using PBS-moistened cotton swabs.
Remove excess subcutaneous fat tissue surrounding the femoral artery with bipolar forceps, taking care to cauterize any blood vessel.
Gently cut the remaining pads of subcutaneous adipose tissue.
Avoid bleeding by gently tapping with bipolar forceps during the cauterization process.
If necrotic tissue is burned, remove it with surgical scissors.
Be careful when performing the incision and removing subcutaneous fat.
Use an electrocauterization device to control bleeding from blood vessels in the fat pad tissue.
Gently extend the incision through the skin until reaching the popliteal bifurcation.
Use straight Micro-Mosquito tweezers to clamp and flip the inguinal muscle for better visualization of the upper extremity of the vasculature.
Identify the inguinal ligament as a reference point.
Dissect the femoral artery and vein using PBS-moistened cotton swabs to brush away surrounding connective tissue.
Place a Forceps clamp to retain the fat pad in place, aiding better visualization of the femoral artery.
Carefully dissect and separate the femoral nerve from the femoral artery and vein using fine forceps.
Carefully separate and dissect the femoral artery and vein from the lateral muscular planes.
Dissect the femoral nerve to clearly distinguish it from the artery and vein.
Pass the closed tip of a curved fine forceps underneath the femoral artery and vein.
Perform electrocauterization after placing the forceps.
Remove the cauterized portion of the vessels with scissors.
Tap 1 cm of the femoral artery and vein for electrocauterization.
Cauterize the vessels between the inguinal ligament and the popliteal bifurcation.
Ensure that cauterization time does not exceed 10 seconds per application.
Clean the area with PBS-moistened cotton swabs to remove any blood leakage.
Check for correct removal of the femoral artery and vein, ensuring no leaks or clots are present.
Remove the clamp from the tissue and moisten with PBS to reduce necrosis.
Close the incision using a surgical stapler with sterilized clips.
Remove mice from the flow of isoflurane® after completing the HLI procedure.
Place the mouse on top of a draped heated pad in a recovery cage.
Monitor continuously until the mouse wakes up from isoflurane®.
Inject analgesic 2 hours post-ischemia to avoid discomfort.
Inject analgesic 24 hours post-ischemia to minimize distress and pain.
Place the mouse on a 37°C heated surface with a non-reflective, light-absorbing surface in the supine position.
Induce sedation by placing the animal in an induction chamber saturated with 5% isoflurane.
Transfer the animal to the table in a supine position.
Place a mask on the animal delivering 1–3% isoflurane in 100% O2 at a flow rate of 1L/min.
Gently extend the ischemic and non-ischemic hind limbs to the same length.
Place the palms of the feet upwards and secure them with tape underneath.
Switch on the PeriScan PIM II Opto-Isolation Unit.
Switch on the computer and initialize the acquisition software (PeriScan System Software – LDPIwin).
Select and click the “Mark Area button” to show the boundaries of the scanned area.
Ensure that both the ischemic and non-ischemic legs are recorded in the same field of scan.
Start the acquisition by clicking “Start”.
Avoid performing the scanning under strong direct ambient light.
Acquire multiple scans of each sample for perfusion analysis.
Set the perfusion scale to a specific range to compensate for background noise and facilitate data comparison between different animals.
Save the file after completing data acquisition.
Return the animal to the recovery cage upon completion of recording.
Monitor the animal continuously until it regains consciousness from isoflurane®.
Collect gastrocnemius (GN) and semimembranosus (SM) muscles 21 days post-HLI for histopathological assessment.
Perform eosin-hematoxylin (H & E) staining for muscle injury evaluation.
Conduct immunofluorescence to quantify post-ischemic angiogenesis.
Humanely sacrifice the mouse.
Make a small incision along the skin of the lower leg around the ankle.
Tear off the entire skin covering the leg.
Perform a small incision on the ankle for gastrocnemius collection.
Firmly pull the skin to expose the underlying skeletal muscle.
Reverse the animal and insert tweezers between the bone and calcaneal tendon to detach the gastrocnemius.
Keep the tweezers in place to assist with cutting the tendon.
Lift the gastrocnemius from the distal portion of the tendon to reveal the soleus muscle.
Gently split the soleus from the gastrocnemius.
Cut the gastrocnemius.
Obtain a cross-sectional view of the trimmed gastrocnemius.
Obtain a lateral view of the trimmed gastrocnemius.
Expose the posterior portion of the tight, revealing the sciatic nerve for semimembranosus collection.
Indicate the portion of the semimembranosus muscle to be harvested in the ventral view.
Gently separate the calcaneal tendon from the bone.
Clamp the tendon very distally underneath the heel using forceps.
Cut the tendon with scissors.
Pull and separate the posterior gastrocnemius muscle from the bone with the forceps.
Dissect the soleus, identified by its bright red color, from the posterior muscle by pulling it from its proximal tendon until the distal tendon is reached.
Cut out the soleus using scissors.
Remove the posterior portion of the tight tissue to expose the sciatic nerve.
Flip the animal ventrally.
Remove a portion of the semimembranosus muscle.
Handle the dissected semimembranosus muscle gently to preserve structural integrity.
Store the dissected gastrocnemius muscle for further histological studies.
Fix the muscles immediately after collection in pH 7, buffered with 4% paraformaldehyde solution for 24 hours in a cold room (4°C).
Dehydrate the muscles in ascending ethanol solutions: 50%, 70%, 80%, and finally 100% by placing the muscle in a 24-well cell culture plate.
Keep the muscles in each solution for 10 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C) with low agitation.
Immerse the samples in xylene three times by placing the muscle in a 24-well cell culture plate.
Keep the muscles in each solution for 10 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C) with low agitation.
Trim the muscle to avoid samples thicker than 4 mm.
Place the samples in the embedding cassette.
Immerse the samples in paraffin at 56°C overnight (16–18 h), or use an automated inclusion machine.
Transfer the muscle sample into the mold using warm forceps, placing the cut side down.
Pour paraffin to embed the sample in the block and let it solidify overnight (16–18 h).
Store the samples at room temperature (22°C–25°C) if not sectioned immediately.
Cool the paraffin blocks at −20°C for 30 min before sectioning or place in slushed crushed ice for 10 min.
Cut the sample into 10-μm-thick sections using a microtome.
Place the slides on a 60°C heated surface or in an oven to spread out the sections for 5 min.
Remove paraffin with 3 washes of p-Xylene for 5 min each.
Rehydrate the sections in decreasing concentrations of ethanol: 100%, 90%, 70%, and 50%.
Clean the samples with PBS 1× for 5 min each.
Immerse the histological sections in hematoxylin for 10 min.
Rinse the slides in tap water for 5 min three times.
Adjust the hematoxylin staining time according to tissue or batch of hematoxylin.
Immerse sections in basic water solution (pH 9) from H&E kit.
Wash tissue in running tap water for 5 min.
Immerse sections in eosin for 1 min.
Rinse slides in tap water for 5 min.
Dehydrate histological section in increasing concentrations of ethanol, 50%, 70% and 100% for 5 min each by dipping the slides in coplin jar.
Drain excess ethanol gently tapping the slides on a paper towel.
Rinse slide in coplin jar containing xylol for three times, 5 min each.
Drain excess xylol.
Mount slides by adding 10 μL of xylol-based mounting buffer on each tissue portion.
Add coverslip and let the slides dry completely.
Embed the tissues immediately in OCT after removing the GN and SM muscles.
Freeze the embedded tissues in nitrogen-cooled isopentane.
Store the frozen tissues at −80°C.
Fix the whole muscle in 4% PFA for 45 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C).
Immerse the fixed muscle in 30% Sucrose in PBS 1× overnight (16–18 hours).
Freeze the sucrose-treated muscle in liquid nitrogen-cooled isopentane.
Store samples at −20°C for up to 2 years if needed.
Cut cryopreserved GN and SM muscles into 10-μm-thick transverse sections using a cryostat.
Store the sections at −80°C for long-term storage.
Bring the sections to room temperature (22°C–25°C) before immunofluorescence.
Wash the sections in a Coplin jar with 1× PBS for 5 minutes.
Fix the tissues in 4% PFA for 10 minutes at room temperature (22°C–25°C).
Wash the fixed tissues twice with 1× PBS for 5 minutes each.
Incubate the sections with a blocking solution for 1 hour at room temperature in a black humidified chamber.
Use a pap pen to prevent mixing of reagents and reduce blocking solution volume.
Incubate the sections with different primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution overnight at 4°C.
Wash sections twice for 5 minutes in a coplin jar containing 1× PBS at room temperature.
Incubate sections with the proper secondary antibody for 1 hour at room temperature in a dark and black humidified chamber.
Dip sections three times in a coplin jar containing 1× PBS.
Incubate sections with DAPI for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark humidified chamber.
Mount sections using Fluoromount-G and coverslips.
Store stained sections at 4°C in a dry box in the dark for a minimum of 24 hours.
Acquire immunofluorescence images with an inverted widefield fluorescence microscope.
Take images at 20× and 40× magnification with oil immersion objectives.
